facts.text: Forest Hill began attracting plantation owners in the mid‑19th century who sought relief from the lowland heat and floods of central Louisiana.
The arrival of railroads from Alexandria southward in the 1890s turned Forest Hill into a logging hub, though it wasn’t incorporated until 1929.
By the 1920s, exhaustive clear‑cutting had depleted old‑growth forests, leading to the closure of sawmills such as Long Leaf and McNary.
Every third weekend of March, Forest Hill hosts the Louisiana Nursery Festival, celebrating its status as one of the state’s oldest and largest nursery regions.
Spring Hill Baptist Church, co‑founded by Ford around 1841, reflects Forest Hill’s early religious consolidation among Anglo‑American migrants.
